stimulus.text:
Passage A — Thomas Jefferson to James Madison, Paris, January 30, 1787: “I hold it that a little rebellion now and then is a good thing, & as necessary in the political world as storms in the physical. . . . It is a medecine necessary for the sound health of government.” (spelling as in the original)
Passage B — George Washington to Henry Lee, Jr., October 31, 1786: “Influence is no government. Let us have one by which our lives, liberties, and properties will be secured, or let us know the worst at once.”
stimulus.source_note: Thomas Jefferson to James Madison, January 30, 1787; George Washington to Henry Lee, Jr., October 31, 1786. Public domain.

options.text: the farmers in Massachusetts had real grievances against the state
options.misconception: Background: in the full letter Washington says to learn what the insurgents aim at and redress real grievances, so he does not deny them.

the rebellion should be punished at all by the government

options.misconception: Neither passage is about western land claims.

rationales.B: Washington says the tumults show the need for a government that can secure lives, liberties, and properties, while Jefferson says a little rebellion is a good and necessary thing, so the two draw opposite lessons from the same unrest.
rationales.A: Background: in the full letter Washington says to learn what the insurgents aim at, so he does not deny their grievances.
rationales.C: Background: both men accept punishment in some form: Jefferson mild punishment, Washington force if there are no grievances.
rationales.D: Neither passage discusses western land claims.
rationales.general:
1. Compare the lessons. Washington wants a government strong enough to secure order.
2. Jefferson calls the same rebellion a good and necessary thing.
3. One man reads unrest as a warning; the other reads it as health.
4. Background: Washington watched from Mount Vernon while Jefferson wrote from Paris, and distance shaped both views.
Remember: the same rebellion can be a crisis to one founder and a cure to another.
